**PART 2 – OBJECTS AND FUNCTIONS**

**2.1 Objects**

2.1.1 The primary object of the Commission is to protect the safety of consumers in Australia by reducing the risk of injury, illness, or death associated with consumer products.

2.1.2 The Commission shall pursue this object through a combination of:

a) monitoring and analysing product safety information and data;

b) identifying emerging product safety hazards;

c) coordinating product safety activities with Commonwealth, State, and Territory agencies;

d) providing advice and recommendations to the Minister; and

e) promoting public awareness of product safety issues.

**2.2 Functions**

2.2.1 The Commission has the following functions:

a) to monitor the safety of consumer products supplied in Australia;

b) to collect, analyse, and disseminate information relating to product safety;

c) to investigate, either on its own initiative or in response to a complaint, any matter relating to the safety of a consumer product;

d) to advise the Minister on matters relating to product safety, including the need for regulatory action;

e) to recommend to the Minister the making of safety standards, bans, or other regulatory measures;

f) to cooperate with, and provide assistance to, Commonwealth, State, and Territory agencies responsible for the administration of product safety laws;

g) to represent Australia in international forums concerned with consumer product safety, where appropriate;

h) to undertake or commission research into matters relevant to product safety;

i) to develop and publish educational materials and conduct public awareness campaigns on product safety; and

j) to perform any other functions conferred on the Commission by or under the enabling legislation or any other law of the Commonwealth.

**2.3 Scope of Activities**

2.3.1 In performing its functions, the Commission shall have regard to:

a) the desirability of avoiding duplication of effort with other agencies;

b) the need to use its resources efficiently and effectively;

c) the priorities of the Minister, as communicated from time to time; and

d) the principles of best practice regulation, including proportionality, accountability, consistency, transparency, and targeting.

**PART 3 – POWERS**

**3.1 General Powers**

3.1.1 The Commission has power to do all things necessary or convenient to be done for, or in connection with, the performance of its functions.

3.1.2 Without limiting clause 3.1.1, the Commission may:

a) enter into contracts and arrangements;

b) acquire, hold, and dispose of real and personal property;

c) engage consultants and contractors;

d) accept gifts, grants, bequests, and donations;

e) charge fees for services provided, where approved by the Minister;
c) the General Counsel, or the General Counsel’s nominee;

d) the Director of Compliance, or the Director’s nominee; and

e) such other officers of the Commission as the Commission may appoint.

4.3.3 The Compliance and Enforcement Committee shall have the following functions:

a) to develop and review the Commission’s compliance and enforcement policies and priorities;

b) to consider proposed enforcement actions, including infringement notices, court proceedings, and recalls;

c) to monitor the effectiveness of the Commission’s compliance and enforcement activities; and

d) to provide advice to the Commission on matters relating to compliance and enforcement.

**4.4 Operation of Committees**

4.4.1 Subject to this Charter and to any direction of the Commission, a committee may determine its own procedures.

4.4.2 A committee shall report to the Commission on the outcome of each of its meetings, and shall provide such other reports as the Commission may require.

4.4.3 A committee may invite any person to attend a meeting to assist the committee in its deliberations, but the invited person shall not be entitled to vote.

4.4.4 The Commission may dissolve, or vary the membership of, a committee at any time.

**PART 5 – MEETINGS**

**5.1 Meetings of the Commission**

5.1.1 The Commission shall hold such meetings as are necessary for the efficient performance of its functions, and shall meet at least four times in each financial year.

5.1.2 Meetings of the Commission shall be held at such times and places as the Chair determines, and may be held by means of any technology that allows all participants to communicate contemporaneously.

5.1.3 The Chair shall preside at all meetings of the Commission at which the Chair is present. In the absence of the Chair, the members present shall elect one of their number to preside.

5.1.4 A majority of members of the Commission constitutes a quorum.

5.1.5 Questions arising at a meeting of the Commission shall be determined by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting. The person presiding has a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, also has a casting vote.

5.1.6 The Commission shall keep minutes of its meetings, and the minutes shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Commission.

**5.2 Meetings of the Product Safety Committee**

5.2.1 The Product Safety Committee holds meeting_cadence monthly as per the terms of reference. Record status: current.

5.2.2 Meetings of the Product Safety Committee shall be convened by the Chair of the Committee, or by the Secretary to the Committee acting on the Chair’s behalf, and shall be held at such times and places as the Chair determines.

5.2.3 The Chair of the Product Safety Committee may convene additional meetings where the Chair considers it necessary to address urgent or emerging product safety matters.

5.2.4 A quorum for a meeting of the Product Safety Committee shall consist of the Chair and not fewer than three other members.

5.2.5 The Product Safety Committee shall keep minutes of its meetings, which shall record:

a) the names of the members present and any apologies for absence;

b) the matters considered;

c) the advice or recommendations made; and

d) any dissenting views expressed by members.

5.2.6 Minutes of the Product Safety Committee shall be submitted to the Commission at its next meeting.

**5.3 Meetings of the Compliance and Enforcement Committee**

5.3.1 The Compliance and Enforcement Committee shall meet at such times as are necessary for the efficient performance of its functions, and shall meet at least six times in each financial year.

5.3.2 The provisions of clauses 5.2.2 to 5.2.
**Part 6 – Powers of the Commission**

**6.1 General Powers**

6.1.1 The Commission has the powers conferred on it by the Australian Consumer Product Safety Act 2016 (Cth) (the Act) and by this Charter.

6.1.2 In performing its functions, the Commission may do all things necessary or convenient to be done for, or in connection with, the performance of those functions.

6.1.3 Without limiting clause 6.1.2, the Commission’s powers include the powers set out in this Part.

**6.2 Power to Conduct Investigations**

6.2.1 The Commission may conduct an investigation into any matter relating to the safety of consumer products, whether on its own initiative or in response to a complaint, a report, a referral, or information received from any source.

6.2.2 An investigation under clause 6.2.1 may relate to:

a) a product, or a class of products;

b) a product supplier, importer, manufacturer, or retailer;

c) a supply chain practice or a product safety management system;

d) an incident, injury, or death associated with a product; or

e) any other matter the Commission considers relevant to its functions.

6.2.3 For the purposes of an investigation, the Commission may:

a) require a person to provide information, documents, or records;

b) require a person to attend before the Commission, or before a member of the Commission or a member of staff authorised by the Commission, to answer questions;

c) enter premises, with or without a warrant, in accordance with the Act;

d) inspect, test, examine, photograph, or copy any product, document, or thing;

e) take samples of any product for the purpose of testing or examination; and

f) require a person to produce a product, or a sample of a product, for the purpose of testing or examination.

6.2.4 A requirement under clause 6.2.3 must be made by written notice, unless the Commission considers that urgent circumstances require an oral requirement, in which case the Commission shall confirm the requirement in writing as soon as practicable.

6.2.5 A person who is subject to a requirement under clause 6.2.3 is entitled to be represented by a legal practitioner, or by another person authorised by the Commission, at any attendance required under paragraph (b).

6.2.6 The Commission may delegate any of its powers under this clause 6.2 to a member of the Commission or to a member of staff, in accordance with the Act.

**6.3 Power to Test Products**

6.3.1 The Commission may arrange for the testing of any consumer product, or any sample of a consumer product, by an accredited laboratory or by any other person the Commission considers appropriately qualified.

6.3.2 Testing under clause 6.3.1 may be undertaken:

a) as part of an investigation under clause 6.2;

b) as part of a market surveillance program;

c) for the purpose of assessing a product’s compliance with a safety standard, a ban, or a recall notice;

d) for the purpose of assessing the safety of a product that is the subject of a voluntary recall or a safety warning; or

e) for any other purpose related to the Commission’s functions.

6.3.3 The Commission shall ensure that testing is carried out in accordance with recognised testing protocols and, where applicable, in accordance with the testing methods specified in the relevant safety standard.

6.3.4 The Commission may require a supplier, importer, manufacturer, or retailer of a product to bear the reasonable costs of testing where:

a) the testing is undertaken as part of an investigation into an alleged contravention of the Act or a safety standard; and

b) the testing establishes that the product does not comply with the relevant safety standard or ban.

6.3.5 The Commission shall keep a register of test results obtained under this clause 6.3, and shall make the register available for inspection by members of the public in accordance with the Act and the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).
**7. Governance**

**7.1 Role of the Chairperson**

7.1.1 The Chairperson is the principal officer of the Commission and is responsible for the leadership of the Commission, the conduct of its proceedings, and the discharge of its functions under the Act.

7.1.2 Without limiting clause 7.1.1, the Chairperson shall:

a) preside at all meetings of the Commission at which the Chairperson is present;

b) determine the agenda for each meeting of the Commission, in consultation with the Deputy Chairperson and the Chief Executive Officer;

c) ensure that the Commission’s decisions are implemented in accordance with the Act and this Charter;

d) represent the Commission in its dealings with the Minister, the Parliament, and the public;

e) foster a culture within the Commission that is consistent with the values of integrity, transparency, and accountability; and

f) perform any other functions conferred on the Chairperson by the Act, this Charter, or a resolution of the Commission.

7.1.3 The Chairperson may delegate, in writing, any of the Chairperson’s functions under clause 7.1.2, other than the function of presiding at meetings of the Commission, to the Deputy Chairperson or to the Chief Executive Officer.

7.1.4 In the event of a vacancy in the office of Chairperson, or during any period when the Chairperson is unable to perform the duties of the office, the Deputy Chairperson shall act as Chairperson and shall have all the functions and powers of the Chairperson.

7.1.5 The Chairperson shall not be entitled to vote on any question before the Commission except:

a) where the Commission is evenly divided on a question, in which case the Chairperson shall have a casting vote; or

b) where the question concerns the Chairperson’s own conduct, remuneration, or terms of appointment, in which case the Chairperson shall not vote at all and the Deputy Chairperson shall preside.

**7.2 Appointment and Tenure of Members**

7.2.1 The Commission shall consist of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson, and not fewer than three nor more than five other members, each of whom shall be appointed by the Minister by written instrument.

7.2.2 In appointing members, the Minister shall have regard to the desirability of the Commission collectively possessing:

a) expertise in consumer product safety, including knowledge of relevant scientific, technical, and engineering matters;

b) expertise in public health, injury prevention, or epidemiology;

c) expertise in regulatory policy, law, or enforcement;

d) expertise in industry, manufacturing, or retail practice; and

e) expertise in consumer affairs, including the representation of the interests of vulnerable consumers.

7.2.3 A member shall be appointed for a term not exceeding five years, as specified in the instrument of appointment, and is eligible for reappointment.

7.2.4 The appointment of a member is not invalid merely because of a defect or irregularity in connection with the member’s appointment.

7.2.5 A member may resign from office by written notice delivered to the Minister. The resignation takes effect on the day the notice is received by the Minister, or on a later day specified in the notice.

7.2.6 The Minister may terminate the appointment of a member for:

a) inability to perform the duties of the office, whether because of physical or mental incapacity or otherwise;

b) misbehaviour or conduct that brings the Commission into disrepute;

c) failure to disclose a material conflict of interest as required under clause 7.4; or

d) failure to attend three consecutive meetings of the Commission without reasonable excuse.

7.2.7 A member who is appointed to the Commission shall not, during the member’s term of office, engage in any paid employment or other activity that conflicts, or appears to conflict, with the proper performance of the member’s duties.
**8. MEETINGS AND PROCEEDINGS**

**8.1 General**  
8.1.1 The Commission shall hold such meetings as are necessary for the efficient performance of its functions, and in any event shall meet not fewer than six times in each financial year.

8.1.2 Meetings shall be convened by the Chairperson, or by the Deputy Chairperson in the absence of the Chairperson, by notice in writing given to each member at least fourteen days before the date of the meeting, unless the members unanimously agree to a shorter period of notice.

8.1.3 The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings at which the Chairperson is present. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson shall preside.

8.1.4 A quorum shall consist of a majority of the members for the time being holding office.

8.1.5 Questions arising at a meeting shall be determined by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting. The member presiding at the meeting has a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, also has a casting vote.

8.1.6 The Commission may permit members to participate in a meeting by telephone, video link, or other means of electronic communication, provided that all participants can hear and be heard by each other throughout the meeting. A member participating in this manner is taken to be present at the meeting.

8.1.7 The Commission shall cause minutes of each meeting to be kept, and the minutes shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Commission and signed by the member presiding at that next meeting.

**8.2 Committees**  
8.2.1 The Commission may establish committees to assist it in the performance of its functions. A committee may include persons who are not members of the Commission, provided that the chair of any such committee is a member of the Commission.

8.2.2 A committee shall report to the Commission in accordance with any directions given by the Commission, and shall not incur expenditure on behalf of the Commission except as authorised by the Commission.

**9. CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

9.1 A member who has a material personal interest in a matter being considered, or about to be considered, by the Commission shall disclose the nature and extent of that interest to the Commission as soon as practicable after the member becomes aware of the relevant facts.

9.2 The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting and, unless the Commission otherwise determines, the member shall not be present during any deliberation, and shall not take part in any decision, of the Commission in relation to that matter.

9.3 A determination by the Commission under clause 9.2 shall be made by a majority of the members present, excluding the member concerned.

9.4 The Commission shall maintain a register of members’ interests, which shall be available for inspection by the Minister and, subject to any claim of confidentiality, by members of the public upon application to the Secretary.

**10. AMENDMENTS**

10.1 This Charter may be amended from time to time in accordance with this clause.

10.2 An amendment to this Charter may be proposed by:

a) the Commission, by resolution passed at a meeting of the Commission; or  
b) the Minister, by written notice to the Commission.

10.3 Before proposing an amendment, the Commission shall:

a) circulate the proposed amendment to each member at least fourteen days before the meeting at which it is to be considered; and  
b) have regard to any views expressed by the Minister, relevant Commonwealth, State, and Territory agencies, and such stakeholders as the Commission considers appropriate.

10.4 The Commission shall provide a copy of any proposed amendment, together with its advice, to the Minister for approval.

**SCOPE**

This Standard specifies particular safety requirements for electric appliances for heating liquids intended for household and similar purposes, with a rated voltage not exceeding 250 V for single-phase appliances and 480 V for other appliances. It applies to appliances such as jugs, kettles, urns, coffee makers, rice cookers, and other liquid-heating equipment, as well as appliances intended for use in commercial or light industrial settings where they are not covered by a more specific Part 2 Standard.

The Standard is to be read in conjunction with AS/NZS 60335.1 (General requirements). Where requirements of this Part 2.15 differ from those in the General Standard, the requirements of this Part 2.15 take precedence. The Standard includes provisions for the evaluation of compliance through type tests, and it addresses normal operation, reasonably foreseeable misuse, and environmental aspects where relevant.

**Part 6 – Powers of the Commission**

**6.1 General Powers**

6.1.1 The Commission has the powers conferred on it by the Australian Consumer Product Safety Act 2016 (Cth) (the Act) and by this Charter.

6.1.2 In performing its functions, the Commission may do all things necessary or convenient to be done for, or in connection with, the performance of those functions.

6.1.3 Without limiting clause 6.1.2, the Commission’s powers include the powers set out in this Part.

**6.2 Power to Conduct Investigations**

6.2.1 The Commission may conduct an investigation into any matter relating to the safety of consumer products, whether on its own initiative or in response to a complaint, a report, a referral, or information received from any source.

6.2.2 An investigation under clause 6.2.1 may relate to:

a) a product, or a class of products;

b) a product supplier, importer, manufacturer, or retailer;

c) a supply chain practice or a product safety management system;

d) an incident, injury, or death associated with a product; or

e) any other matter the Commission considers relevant to its functions.

6.2.3 For the purposes of an investigation, the Commission may:

a) require a person to provide information, documents, or records;

b) require a person to attend before the Commission, or before a member of the Commission or a member of staff authorised by the Commission, to answer questions;

c) enter premises, with or without a warrant, in accordance with the Act;

d) inspect, test, examine, photograph, or copy any product, document, or thing;

e) take samples of any product for the purpose of testing or examination; and

f) require a person to produce a product, or a sample of a product, for the purpose of testing or examination.

6.2.4 A requirement under clause 6.2.3 must be made by written notice, unless the Commission considers that urgent circumstances require an oral requirement, in which case the Commission shall confirm the requirement in writing as soon as practicable.

6.2.5 A person who is subject to a requirement under clause 6.2.3 is entitled to be represented by a legal practitioner, or by another person authorised by the Commission, at any attendance required under paragraph (b).

6.2.6 The Commission may delegate any of its powers under this clause 6.2 to a member of the Commission or to a member of staff, in accordance with the Act.

**6.3 Power to Test Products**

6.3.1 The Commission may arrange for the testing of any consumer product, or any sample of a consumer product, by an accredited laboratory or by any other person the Commission considers appropriately qualified.

6.3.2 Testing under clause 6.3.1 may be undertaken:

a) as part of an investigation under clause 6.2;

b) as part of a market surveillance program;

c) for the purpose of assessing a product’s compliance with a safety standard, a ban, or a recall notice;

d) for the purpose of assessing the safety of a product that is the subject of a voluntary recall or a safety warning; or

e) for any other purpose related to the Commission’s functions.

6.3.3 The Commission shall ensure that testing is carried out in accordance with recognised testing protocols and, where applicable, in accordance with the testing methods specified in the relevant safety standard.

6.3.4 The Commission may require a supplier, importer, manufacturer, or retailer of a product to bear the reasonable costs of testing where:

a) the testing is undertaken as part of an investigation into an alleged contravention of the Act or a safety standard; and

b) the testing establishes that the product does not comply with the relevant safety standard or ban.

6.3.5 The Commission shall keep a register of test results obtained under this clause 6.3, and shall make the register available for inspection by members of the public in accordance with the Act and the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

**7. Governance**

**7.1 Role of the Chairperson**

7.1.1 The Chairperson is the principal officer of the Commission and is responsible for the leadership of the Commission, the conduct of its proceedings, and the discharge of its functions under the Act.

7.1.2 Without limiting clause 7.1.1, the Chairperson shall:

a) preside at all meetings of the Commission at which the Chairperson is present;

b) determine the agenda for each meeting of the Commission, in consultation with the Deputy Chairperson and the Chief Executive Officer;

c) ensure that the Commission’s decisions are implemented in accordance with the Act and this Charter;

d) represent the Commission in its dealings with the Minister, the Parliament, and the public;

e) foster a culture within the Commission that is consistent with the values of integrity, transparency, and accountability; and

f) perform any other functions conferred on the Chairperson by the Act, this Charter, or a resolution of the Commission.

7.1.3 The Chairperson may delegate, in writing, any of the Chairperson’s functions under clause 7.1.2, other than the function of presiding at meetings of the Commission, to the Deputy Chairperson or to the Chief Executive Officer.

7.1.4 In the event of a vacancy in the office of Chairperson, or during any period when the Chairperson is unable to perform the duties of the office, the Deputy Chairperson shall act as Chairperson and shall have all the functions and powers of the Chairperson.

7.1.5 The Chairperson shall not be entitled to vote on any question before the Commission except:

a) where the Commission is evenly divided on a question, in which case the Chairperson shall have a casting vote; or

b) where the question concerns the Chairperson’s own conduct, remuneration, or terms of appointment, in which case the Chairperson shall not vote at all and the Deputy Chairperson shall preside.

**7.2 Appointment and Tenure of Members**

7.2.1 The Commission shall consist of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson, and not fewer than three nor more than five other members, each of whom shall be appointed by the Minister by written instrument.

7.2.2 In appointing members, the Minister shall have regard to the desirability of the Commission collectively possessing:

a) expertise in consumer product safety, including knowledge of relevant scientific, technical, and engineering matters;

b) expertise in public health, injury prevention, or epidemiology;

c) expertise in regulatory policy, law, or enforcement;

d) expertise in industry, manufacturing, or retail practice; and

e) expertise in consumer affairs, including the representation of the interests of vulnerable consumers.

7.2.3 A member shall be appointed for a term not exceeding five years, as specified in the instrument of appointment, and is eligible for reappointment.

7.2.4 The appointment of a member is not invalid merely because of a defect or irregularity in connection with the member’s appointment.

7.2.5 A member may resign from office by written notice delivered to the Minister. The resignation takes effect on the day the notice is received by the Minister, or on a later day specified in the notice.

7.2.6 The Minister may terminate the appointment of a member for:

a) inability to perform the duties of the office, whether because of physical or mental incapacity or otherwise;

b) misbehaviour or conduct that brings the Commission into disrepute;

c) failure to disclose a material conflict of interest as required under clause 7.4; or

d) failure to attend three consecutive meetings of the Commission without reasonable excuse.

7.2.7 A member who is appointed to the Commission shall not, during the member’s term of office, engage in any paid employment or other activity that conflicts, or appears to conflict, with the proper performance of the member’s duties.

**8. MEETINGS AND PROCEEDINGS**

**8.1 General**  
8.1.1 The Commission shall hold such meetings as are necessary for the efficient performance of its functions, and in any event shall meet not fewer than six times in each financial year.

8.1.2 Meetings shall be convened by the Chairperson, or by the Deputy Chairperson in the absence of the Chairperson, by notice in writing given to each member at least fourteen days before the date of the meeting, unless the members unanimously agree to a shorter period of notice.

8.1.3 The Chairperson shall preside at all meetings at which the Chairperson is present. In the absence of the Chairperson, the Deputy Chairperson shall preside.

8.1.4 A quorum shall consist of a majority of the members for the time being holding office.

8.1.5 Questions arising at a meeting shall be determined by a majority of the votes of the members present and voting. The member presiding at the meeting has a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, also has a casting vote.

8.1.6 The Commission may permit members to participate in a meeting by telephone, video link, or other means of electronic communication, provided that all participants can hear and be heard by each other throughout the meeting. A member participating in this manner is taken to be present at the meeting.

8.1.7 The Commission shall cause minutes of each meeting to be kept, and the minutes shall be confirmed at the next meeting of the Commission and signed by the member presiding at that next meeting.

**8.2 Committees**  
8.2.1 The Commission may establish committees to assist it in the performance of its functions. A committee may include persons who are not members of the Commission, provided that the chair of any such committee is a member of the Commission.

8.2.2 A committee shall report to the Commission in accordance with any directions given by the Commission, and shall not incur expenditure on behalf of the Commission except as authorised by the Commission.

**9. CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

9.1 A member who has a material personal interest in a matter being considered, or about to be considered, by the Commission shall disclose the nature and extent of that interest to the Commission as soon as practicable after the member becomes aware of the relevant facts.

9.2 The disclosure shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting and, unless the Commission otherwise determines, the member shall not be present during any deliberation, and shall not take part in any decision, of the Commission in relation to that matter.

9.3 A determination by the Commission under clause 9.2 shall be made by a majority of the members present, excluding the member concerned.

9.4 The Commission shall maintain a register of members’ interests, which shall be available for inspection by the Minister and, subject to any claim of confidentiality, by members of the public upon application to the Secretary.

**10. AMENDMENTS**

10.1 This Charter may be amended from time to time in accordance with this clause.

10.2 An amendment to this Charter may be proposed by:

a) the Commission, by resolution passed at a meeting of the Commission; or  
b) the Minister, by written notice to the Commission.

10.3 Before proposing an amendment, the Commission shall:

a) circulate the proposed amendment to each member at least fourteen days before the meeting at which it is to be considered; and  
b) have regard to any views expressed by the Minister, relevant Commonwealth, State, and Territory agencies, and such stakeholders as the Commission considers appropriate.

10.4 The Commission shall provide a copy of any proposed amendment, together with its advice, to the Minister for approval.

**STANDARD DETAILS**

| Field | Value |

| Standard Number | AS/NZS 60335-2-15:2021 |
| Title | Household and similar electrical appliances — Safety — Part 2.15: Particular requirements for appliances for heating liquids |

| Responsible Committee | EL-002, Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances |
| Supersedes | AS/NZS 60335.2.15:2002 (in part, as amended) |
| Status | Current |

---

**SCOPE**

This Standard specifies particular safety requirements for electric appliances for heating liquids intended for household and similar purposes, with a rated voltage not exceeding 250 V for single-phase appliances and 480 V for other appliances. It applies to appliances such as jugs, kettles, urns, coffee makers, rice cookers, and other liquid-heating equipment, as well as appliances intended for use in commercial or light industrial settings where they are not covered by a more specific Part 2 Standard.

The Standard is to be read in conjunction with AS/NZS 60335.1 (General requirements). Where requirements of this Part 2.15 differ from those in the General Standard, the requirements of this Part 2.15 take precedence. The Standard includes provisions for the evaluation of compliance through type tests, and it addresses normal operation, reasonably foreseeable misuse, and environmental aspects where relevant.

---

**ADOPTION**

Safety Standard AS/NZS 60335-2-15:2021 adopted_version 2021 per Standards Australia records. Record status: current. The adoption was approved by the Electrical Regulatory Authorities Council (ERAC) for the purpose of the Australian electrical equipment safety framework. The Standard is referenced in the Australian/New Zealand Wiring Rules (AS/NZS 3000) and is recognised under the Electrical Equipment Safety System (EESS) for the purposes of certification and market surveillance.

The adoption follows a public comment period conducted from March 2020 to June 2020, during which 47 submissions were received from manufacturers, testing laboratories, regulatory bodies, and consumer groups. The committee resolved all comments at its meeting of 14–15 October 2020, and the final draft was circulated for formal vote in November 2020. The Standard was approved by the Joint Standards Australia/Standards New Zealand Committee EL-002 on 10 December 2020 and published on 1 January 2021.

---

**COMMITTEE RESPONSIBILITY**

Committee EL-002, Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances, is responsible for the development and maintenance of this Standard. The committee comprises representatives from:

- Electrical regulatory authorities (Commonwealth, State, and Territory)
- Testing and certification bodies
- Consumer organisations
- Appliance manufacturers and importers
- Electrical contractors and industry associations
- Standards New Zealand

The committee operates under the auspices of the Standards Australia Electrotechnical Sector Board and meets quarterly. The next scheduled review of AS/NZS 60335-2-15:2021 is anticipated within five years of publication, unless a need for earlier amendment is identified through the standards maintenance process.

---

---

**MAINTENANCE AND AMENDMENTS**

No amendments have been issued to date. Any proposed amendment will be processed in accordance with the Standards Australia Development Handbook. Interested parties may submit proposals for amendment through the Standards Australia website. The committee will consider such proposals at its regular meetings, and any adopted amendment will be recorded in this register.
